⁣
Few films blur the line between on-screen chemistry and real-life history quite like La Piscine. The film reunited Alain Delon and Romy Schneider, once one of European cinema’s most famous couples. They had fallen in love years earlier, became engaged, and eventually separated. By the time La Piscine was made, Schneider had married actor and director Harry Meyen and had a child.⁣
⁣
Delon personally pushed for Schneider to play Marianne opposite him. Their complicated history gave the film something that couldn’t easily be manufactured. Every look between them seems loaded with familiarity, attraction and resentment. The exact emotions that drive the story.⁣
⁣
Set almost entirely around a luxurious villa and swimming pool in Saint-Tropez, La Piscine begins like a perfect summer escape. Jean-Paul and Marianne spend their days swimming and relaxing in the sun until the arrival of Marianne’s former lover Harry, played by Maurice Ronet, and his daughter Penelope changes everything. Jealousy slowly replaces tranquility, and the beautiful surroundings become increasingly claustrophobic.⁣
⁣
The atmosphere surrounding the production was almost as dramatic. During filming, Delon’s former bodyguard Stevan Marković was found murdered near Paris. The unsolved killing developed into the notorious Marković affair, involving allegations of blackmail, compromising photographs, organized-crime connections and eventually figures close to French political power. Delon was questioned during the investigation but was never charged.⁣
⁣
Decades later, the film carried an entirely different weight for him. Delon said that watching La Piscine had become painful because both Schneider and Ronet had died relatively young. What had once captured three stars at the height of their beauty and fame had become a reminder of people he had lost. That history makes La Piscine even more fascinating today. Beneath the sunshine, beautiful people and blue Mediterranean water is a film built on jealousy, desire and danger. And some of its tension was far more real than audiences could have known.⁣

source_details.synopsis: La Piscine (The Swimming Pool) is a 1969 psychological thriller film directed by Jacques Deray and starring Alain Delon, Romy Schneider, Maurice Ronet and Jane Birkin. Set in summertime on the French Riviera, it is a drama of sexual jealousy and possessiveness. Both French and English-language versions of the film were made, with the actors filmed speaking English for the international release, which was unusual at a time when films were always either dubbed or subtitled. The 114-minute international release, shorter than the French version, also had slightly different editing.
